content: The Centre for Integrated Health Programs (CIHP) in Nigeria, along with experts such as Rachel J. Blacher from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Teagan Callahan from the CDC, Rosalind Carter from UNICEF, Monica Alonso Gonzalez from the Pan American Health Organization, Raul Gonzalez from the World Health Organization (WHO) in Switzerland, and Chika Hayashi from WHO Switzerland, contributed to the development of this guidance. Other contributors include James Houston (CDC, USA), Priscilla Idele (UNICEF, USA), Shabbir Ismail (Elizabeth Glaser Pediatric AIDS Foundation, USA), Hamida Khattabi (WHO Regional Office for Eastern Mediterranean), Karin Lane (USAID, USA), Binod Mahanty (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, Germany), Amaya Maw-Niang (WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia), Lisa Nelson (WHO, Switzerland), Razia Pendse (WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia), Nirina Razakaso (WHO Regional Office for Africa), Nigel Rollins (WHO, Switzerland), Nathan Shaffer (WHO, Switzerland), Annemarie Stengaard (WHO Regional Office for Europe), Fatima Tsiouris (International Center for AIDS Care and Treatment Programs (ICAP), Columbia University, USA), Dongbao Yu (WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia), and UNAIDS staff. The Paediatric ART Working Group included Elaine Abrams (ICAP, Columbia University, USA), Anouk Amzel (USAID, USA), Dick Chamla (UNICEF, USA), Otto Diallo (CDC, USA), Meg Doherty (WHO, Switzerland), Eric Dziuban (CDC, USA), Ruby Fayorsey (ICAP, Columbia University, USA), Jacqueline Firth (USAID, USA), Monica Alonso Gonzalez (Pan American Health Organization), Raul Gonzalez (WHO, Switzerland), Chika Hayashi (WHO, Switzerland), Priscilla Idele (UNICEF, USA), Hamida Khattabi (WHO Regional Office for Eastern Mediterranean), Emilia H. Koumans (CDC, USA), Amaya Maw-Niang (WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia), Lulu Muhe (WHO, Switzerland), Martina Penazzato (WHO, Switzerland), Razia Pendse (WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia), Benjamin Phelps (USAID, USA), Nirina Razakaso (WHO Regional Office for Africa), Tin Tin Sint (UNICEF, USA), Annemarie Stengaard (WHO Regional Office for Europe), Dongbao Yu (WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia), and UNAIDS staff. The HIV Testing and Counselling Group included John Aberle-Grasse (CDC, USA), Rachel Baggaley (WHO, Switzerland), Stephanie Behel (CDC, USA), Charlene Brown (USAID, USA), Kathryn Curran (WHO Consultant, Switzerland), Denise Duran (CDC, USA), Juliette Edzeame (GIZ GmbH, Germany), Monica Alonso Gonzalez (Pan American Health Organization, USA), Chika Hayashi (WHO, Switzerland), Cheryl Johnson (WHO Consultant, Switzerland), Hamida Khattabi (WHO Regional Office for Eastern Mediterranean), Elizabeth Marum (CDC, USA), Amaya Maw-Niang (WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia), Nirina Razakaso (WHO Regional Office for Africa), Kristi Ruutel (National Institute for Health Development, Estonia), Annemarie Stengaard (WHO Regional Office for Europe), Vincent Wong (USAID, USA), Dongbao Yu (WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia), and UNAIDS staff. The Key Population Group included Stefan Baral (Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, USA), Irene Benech (CDC, Tanzania), Gina Dallabetta (Gates Foundation, USA), Txema Calleja (WHO, Switzerland), Monica Alonso Gonzalez (Pan American Health Organization, USA), Annette Verster (WHO, Switzerland), and UNAIDS staff. Additional contributors included B. Rewari (National AIDS Control Organisation, India), Boniswa Sharon Seti (AIDS & Rights Alliance for Southern Africa, South Africa), Seng Sopheap (The National Center for HIV/AIDS, Dermatology and STD Control, Cambodia), Annemarie Stengaard (WHO Regional Office for Europe), Hazim Timimi (WHO, Switzerland), Jeroen van Gorkom (KNCV Tuberculosis Foundation, Netherlands), Eliud Wandwalo (The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria, Switzerland), and UNAIDS staff. The Indicator Review Panel, tasked with reviewing new indicators, included Rachel Albone (HelpAge International, London), Joy Fishel (Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS), USA), Nicole Fraser (World Bank, United Kingdom), David Hales (Indicator expert, United Kingdom), Chika Hayashi (WHO, Switzerland), Jon Hopkins (International Planned Parenthood Federation, United Kingdom), Patrick Kaburi (National AIDS Control Council, Kenya), and Teymur Noori (European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, Sweden). Contributors for Part 2 included John Aberle-Grasse (CDC, USA), Annabel Baddeley (WHO Department of Global Tuberculosis), Rachel Baggaley (WHO Department of HIV), Isabel Bergeri (WHO Department of HIV), Silvia Bertagnolio (WHO Department of HIV), Rachel Blacher (CDC, USA), Alex Cox (CDC, USA), Jacob Dee (CDC, USA), Neelam Dhingra-Kumar (WHO Department of Health Systems and Innovation), Meg Doherty (WHO Department of HIV), Shaffiq Essajee (WHO Department of HIV), Dennis Falzon (WHO Department of Global Tuberculosis), Nathan Ford (WHO Department of HIV), Haileyesus Getahun (WHO Department of Global Tuberculosis), Phillipe Glaziou (WHO Department of Global Tuberculosis), Vincent Habiyambere (WHO Department of HIV), James Houston (CDC, USA), Priscilla Idele (UNICEF, USA), Selma Khamassi (WHO Department of Health Systems and Innovation), Evelyn Kim (CDC, USA), Jeremy Addison Lauer (WHO Department of Health Systems and Innovation), Bradley Mathers (Kirby Institute, Australia), Eyerusalem Negussie (WHO Department of HIV), Lisa Nelson (WHO Department of HIV), Philippa Easterbrook (WHO Department of HIV), Lori Newman (WHO Department of Reproductive Health and Research), Elevanie Nyakesha (UNICEF, USA), Kevin O’Reilly (WHO Department of HIV), Martina Penazzato (WHO Department of HIV), and others. WHO staff and consultants, including Chika Hayashi (Department of HIV), coordinated the overall guideline development process with Daniel Low-Beer (Department of HIV), Gundo Weiler (Department of HIV), and Txema Calleja (Department of HIV). Daniel Tarantola (Consultant, Department of HIV) provided overall guidance on the guide and developed initial drafts of several sections. This group constitutes the WHO Guideline Steering Group. The following WHO staff members contributed to developing the content or drafting sections of the guidelines: Annabel Baddeley (Department of Global Tuberculosis), Rachel Baggaley (Department of HIV), Mazuwa Banda (Department of HIV), Isabel Bergeri (Department of HIV), Silvia Bertagnolio (Department of HIV), Michel Beusenberg (Department of HIV), Meg Doherty (Department of HIV), Philippa Easterbrook (Department of HIV), Dennis Falzon (Department of Global Tuberculosis), Nathan Ford (Department of HIV), Haileyesus Getahun (Department of Global Tuberculosis), Phillipe Glaziou (Department of Global Tuberculosis), Raul Gonzalez (Department of HIV), Monica Alonso Gonzalez (Pan American Health Organization), Vincent Habiyambere (Department of HIV), Masaya Kato (WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific), Hamida Khattabi (WHO Regional Office for Eastern Mediterranean). WHO consultants involved in developing these guidelines included Theresa Babovic, April Baller, Jhoney Barcarolo, Cheryl Johnson, Michael Jordan, Avinash Kanchar, and Michelle Williams. Special thanks go to WHO consultants/writers/editors Ward Rinehart and Sarah Johnson from Jura Editorial Service for developmental editing. Celine Daly provided technical writing and editing throughout the development process. Oyuntungalag Namjilsuren provided communication support. Maryann-Nnenkai Akpama and Laurent Poulain provided additional administrative and management support. Financial support for this work came from The United States President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR). Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH provided financial support for a senior consultant. WHO is also grateful to the institutions that contributed staff time and other in-kind contributions to the guideline development process.
